# Implementation Plan: Dedicated Contact Page & Sanity CMS Scaffold

**Branch**: `002-build-dedicated-contact` | **Date**: 2025-10-31 | **Spec**: `/specs/002-build-dedicated-contact/spec.md`  
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/002-build-dedicated-contact/spec.md`

**Note**: This template is generated by `/speckit.plan`. Every decision recorded here MUST reference the Nyan Cat Space constitution and demonstrate compliance before implementation begins.

## Summary

Ship a first-class contact experience and future-proof blog foundation without breaking the cosmic terminal vibe. The new `contact.html` becomes the primary conversion surface: instead of a hosted form, it offers a frictionless email call-to-action (`mailto:`) plus copy-to-clipboard fallback and clear instructions, all honed for accessibility and reduced-motion preferences. In parallel, scaffold a Sanity.io-powered blog informed by “Using Sanity.io with Vanilla JavaScript for a Static Portfolio Site.pdf”: define datasets, environment variables, and a lightweight client helper so published posts can render on a new `blog.html` while the empty state stays on-brand. Target users include collaborators reaching out via email and readers exploring upcoming blog content; both flows must respect constitution gates for accessibility, performance, and narrative clarity.

## Technical Context

**Languages**: HTML5, Tailwind CSS utilities, vanilla JavaScript (ES2020)  
**Dependencies**: `styles/tailwind.css` (hand-authored utility set); no build tooling, frameworks, or external JS libraries; `mailto:` CTA with optional Clipboard API helper; Sanity Content Lake queried via native `fetch` with GROQ derived from the PDF reference  
**Assets**: Media stored under `assets/`; individual files ≤ 200KB unless a variance is justified in Constitution Check  
**Validation**: Manual accessibility sweeps (keyboard navigation, contrast, reduced motion), responsive testing across mobile/desktop, email CTA smoke test (mailto launch + clipboard fallback), Sanity mock data verification, optional automated linting if available  
**Target Platforms**: Evergreen desktop/mobile browsers, graceful fallback with JavaScript disabled  
**Performance Goals**: First meaningful paint < 2s on LTE, animation frame budgets ≤ 16ms, zero blocking network requests after initial page load; Sanity fetch runs post-load and caches results in-memory  
**Constraints**: Preserve retro terminal aesthetic, respect prefers-reduced-motion, stay fully static (no build tooling), maintain accessible content hierarchy, surface contact instructions that work with and without JavaScript  
**Scope**: Existing static pages plus new `contact.html` and `blog.html`, shared assets, Sanity helper, environment documentation

## Constitution Check

*Gate: MUST pass before Phase 0 research. Re-validate after Phase 1 design.*

- **Terminal Fidelity**: Contact and blog pages reuse the black background + neon palette, monospace typography, and console blocks. Tailwind utilities may add CTA-specific styles while respecting the command-line aesthetic. Navigation items use the same hover/focus glow as existing pages. Inline instructions should read like console output.
- **Cosmic Performance & Simplicity**: No hosted form submissions; contact relies on plain HTML links plus a tiny Clipboard helper (<1 KB). Sanity integration uses a single helper under 2 KB (GZIP) loaded only on `blog.html`. Fetch executes after `DOMContentLoaded` to avoid blocking first paint.  
- **Universal Accessibility**: `contact.html` keeps the skip link target and explicit headings. CTA buttons expose visible focus rings, and clipboard confirmation uses `aria-live`. When scripts are disabled, the email remains selectable text. Blog empty state and post list maintain heading hierarchy (`h1` page title, `h2` per post).  
- **Playful Animation Discipline**: Only subtle hover/focus pulses; no auto-running animations beyond existing starfield/Nyan Cat, which already observe reduced motion. CTA feedback relies on color and outline changes, not motion.  
- **Narrative & Content Clarity**: Navigation points to `contact.html` and `blog.html`, keeping story beats coherent. Contact hero copy references opening a “transmission” via email, and inline notes clarify alternate channels. Blog header frames posts as “captain’s log entries,” aligning with cosmic narrative while clarifying state (published posts vs. empty). Footer and skip link remain intact to preserve flow across breakpoints.
